title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is headed 'Questions sur V.A. et groupes formels'. It records Barsotti's isogeny question, probably as relayed by Manin, along with Grothendieck's partial analysis. The context is the Tate letter of 1966 (Dieudonné modules, crystals, Tate's theorem over finite fields).

Setting: k is algebraically closed of characteristic p>0. A and B are abelian varieties that are 'hypersingulières', meaning they have no points of order p, i.e. p-rank 0. Their formal groups (p-divisible groups) are denoted Ā, B̄.

Q1 (Barsotti): if Ā and B̄ are isogenous, are A and B isogenous?
- For dim 1 this is Deuring: all supersingular elliptic curves over k are isogenous.
- For dim 2, a p-rank-0 surface has Dieudonné–Manin type G_{1,1}+G_{1,1} (Newton slopes all 1/2). So the question becomes: is every p-rank-0 abelian surface isogenous to a product of two supersingular elliptic curves, equivalently to E^2? Manin reportedly did not know, but claimed it for p=2.

Second paragraph: drop the hypothesis 'hypersingulière'. Then there exist simple surfaces A, B with isomorphic non-toroidal formal groups, of type Ĝ_m + G_{1,1} (p-rank 1), that are not isogenous. Grothendieck's argument runs as follows.
- In the 3-dimensional moduli space M_2 of genus-2 Jacobians, those of p-rank ≤1 form a 2-dimensional subfamily N.
- The non-simple members of N are those isogenous to E×F with E ordinary and F supersingular. These form a family of dimension ≤1, because there is no continuous family of varieties isogenous to a fixed E×F.
- On the next page: for a simple A in N, the A' isogenous to A form a discrete (countable) set, all definable over a finite extension of a field of definition of A.
- Hence the transcendence degree over F_p of the field of moduli (0, 1 or 2) is an isogeny invariant. Points of the simple locus U⊂N with different transcendence degrees give simple, formally isomorphic, non-isogenous surfaces.
- Conclusion: the formal (Newton/Dieudonné) isogeny class is strictly coarser than the isogeny class. Barsotti's question can only hope for a positive answer in the supersingular case.
errors: The 'Manin claims it for p=2' attribution is not clearly legible and is unverified.

Grothendieck's dimension-2 reduction implicitly uses the fact that p-rank 0 ⇔ supersingular for surfaces. That is true in dimension 2 but false in dimension ≥3: for g=3, p-rank 0 allows slopes (1/3,2/3). So 'hypersingulière' is the wrong hypothesis for Barsotti's question in general. Even with the right hypothesis (same Newton polygon), the answer is negative outside the supersingular case.

Next page, continuing this argument: 'toute variété isogène à E×F (E ordinaire, F supersingulière) est isomorphe à un produit E'×F'' is false. Take the quotient (E×F)/Γ, with Γ the graph of an isomorphism E[ℓ]≅F[ℓ] (ℓ≠p). This is isogenous to E×F, but its only elliptic subcurves are the images of E and F, which meet in a group of order ℓ². So it is not a product. Indeed, genus-2 Jacobians isogenous to E×F are typically such glued quotients.
Consequently the non-simple locus is a countable union of 1-dimensional families rather than a single closed subfamily. The dimension bound ≤1, and so the conclusion, survive.

The claim that the varieties isogenous to a simple A are definable over a finite extension of k needs 'up to purely inseparable extension'. In the supersingular case the analogous 'discreteness' fails outright, since α_p-quotients give positive-dimensional families inside one isogeny class. Grothendieck correctly restricts to the p-rank-1 case.

ideas.what: Barsotti's question: do isogenous formal groups imply isogenous abelian varieties (p-rank 0)?
ideas.modern_name: Supersingular abelian varieties are isogenous to E^g; formal (Newton) isogeny class vs isogeny class
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (g=1); Tate 1966 over finite fields; Oort 1974 (Invent. Math., 'Subvarieties of moduli spaces') in general for supersingular varieties
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed in correspondence around the 1966 Tate letter; not in EGA/SGA

ideas.what: For g=2, p-rank 0 forces type G_{1,1}+G_{1,1} (supersingular)
ideas.modern_name: Newton polygons in dimension 2 / Dieudonné–Manin classification

ideas.what: Transcendence degree of the field of moduli as an isogeny invariant, used to produce simple, formally isomorphic, non-isogenous surfaces of p-rank 1
ideas.modern_name: Countability of isogeny classes vs dimension of Newton strata; central leaves of positive dimension (Hecke orbits)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oort (foliations, 2004), Chai–Oort (Hecke orbit conjecture); the elementary counting argument is folklore

ideas.what: Dimension count: p-rank ≤1 genus-2 Jacobians form a 2-dimensional family in M_2, non-simple ones a ≤1-dimensional family
ideas.modern_name: p-rank stratification of A_2/M_2; loci of curves with split Jacobians

deep.surprise_reason: These are questions with a sketchy counterexample, all settled in the literature. Oort 1974 shows supersingular varieties are isogenous to E^g. The Chai–Oort leaf theory explains why formal isogeny ≠ isogeny outside the supersingular locus. The transcendence-degree argument is elegant but elementary. The page also carries a minor false claim (continued on the next page) about varieties isogenous to E×F being products. Historically mildly interesting as evidence that Grothendieck engaged with Barsotti/Manin's question around 1966.
transcription_corrections: 'gp formel \widehat{G_{1,0}}[?] + G_{1,1}' is most likely $\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_m + G_{1,1}$ (formal multiplicative group plus G_{1,1}), equivalent to G_{1,0}+G_{1,1} in Manin's notation.
'Il affirme que c'est vrai [?] dans [?] p=2' reads approximately 'Il affirme que c'est vrai en cas p=2' (or 'au cas p=2').
'Soient A, B deux VA sur k alg clos (car p>0)': the parenthesis is 'car p>0' (characteristic p>0).
'sans pts d'ordre p' is confirmed; 'Si [-p-] dim A=1' has a struck-out 'p'.
Next page: 'toute courbe [?] isogène à E×F' should read 'toute variété isogène'.
